title: Stellar nursery NGC 3603
caption: The starburst region NGC 3603, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 3603 · constellation Carina · about 22000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #88 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A star cluster sits amid richly textured clouds of gas and dust in this wide view from ESO's Very Large Telescope. This is NGC 3603, a starburst region, where stars are forming at a furious pace from the nebula's sprawling clouds of gas and dust.

About 22,000 light-years from the Sun, NGC 3603 is the closest known region of its kind in our galaxy. That makes it a valuable local test bed. Intense bursts of star formation like this are very common in other galaxies, but those are so far away that the process is hard to study in detail there.

The image was made with the FORS instrument on one of the four 8.2-meter Unit Telescopes of the VLT at Cerro Paranal in Chile. It combines exposures through three filters, two in visible light and one in the near-infrared, and shows a wide field around the cluster, bringing out the texture of its surroundings.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (8.96 x 9.04 arcminutes) and distance (22000 light years), the frame spans roughly 57 × 58 light-years. Its light set out about 22,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a three-color composite from the FORS instrument on the Very Large Telescope, using visible (V and R) and near-infrared (I) filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Part of the light is near-infrared and invisible to the eye, and the long exposures gather far more light than the eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture spans a field 7 arcminutes wide and was assembled from exposures through the V, R and I filters. NGC 3603 lies in the direction of the constellation Carina, and ESO has also offered the picture as a mounted print in its shop.
alt: A star cluster surrounded by textured clouds of gas and dust.
